The maintenance technician was closing an isolation valve on the overhead compressed air line above the assembly cell. The task was underway because the line was being isolated for a scheduled repair to a leaking fitting downstream. Stage of the task: planned maintenance or servicing. Method in effect: WI-330 Compressed Air Line Isolation. The task was not being performed as written. The difference from the written method was as follows: the written method calls for the valve to be reached from the mobile platform, but the platform was in use on the other side of the plant so a stepladder was used instead. Equipment involved: An 8 foot fiberglass stepladder, asset 20114, and the overhead air line isolation valve. Equipment state at the time: at rest or stopped. Equipment condition: The ladder was in serviceable condition with a current inspection tag and no visible damage. Object handled weighed a pipe wrench of approximately 4 pounds. Object size and shape: about 18 inches long, carried in the right hand. The object was held as follows: held in the right hand while the left hand was on the ladder rail. PPE in use: Safety glasses, steel toe boots and general purpose gloves. This matched the PPE specified for the task. Immediately before the event: standing on the third step of the stepladder with the left hand on the rail, the right arm extended up and out to the left toward the valve, and both feet on the same step. At the moment of the event: the ladder shifted to the left as the reach extended past the side rail, the left foot came off the step, and the fall was taken onto the concrete floor landing on the right foot. Immediately after the event: the wrench was dropped clear, the technician sat on the floor unable to bear weight on the right foot, and a nearby operator called the supervisor. The maintenance technician fell from elevation. Footwear: Site issued steel toe boots in good condition with the tread intact. Carried at the time: A pipe wrench in the right hand, which left only one hand for the ladder. Fall height: approximately 3 feet, from the third step of the stepladder to the concrete floor. Working surface and landing surface: An 8 foot fiberglass stepladder set on sealed concrete with one leg resting partly on a cable tray cover, landing on sealed concrete. Fall protection: No fall protection is required below 6 feet on this site, none was available at the location, and none was in use. The fall was initiated when the ladder shifted to the left as the reach extended out past the side rail toward the valve. Point of contact and direction of force: the right foot contacted the floor first with the ankle rolling outward, force directed upward through the outer ankle. Difference from a normal run of this task: The mobile platform is normally used for this valve and was unavailable, and the cable tray cover made the ladder footing uneven. Conditions at the point of injury: congested or restricted working space and uneven, damaged or obstructed floor. Detail: The floor under the valve carries a cable tray cover about 2 inches proud, so the ladder could not be set level. Timing: About 90 minutes into an 8 hour shift and roughly 5 minutes into this task. The maintenance technician had performed this task before. No known hazard, prior near miss, open action or risk assessment covers this task. No guard, interlock, barrier or control was bypassed, missing, defeated or ineffective. Stop-work opportunity: The job could have waited for the mobile platform to become available, but the repair was scheduled for that morning. First aid at the scene: The right boot was left on and a cold pack was applied to the ankle while waiting for transport. This was given by a trained first aid responder. Notification: The supervisor attended within about a minute and EHS was notified immediately after. Scene and equipment: The ladder was left in place and the area was barriered off until EHS had photographed it. Work at the location stopped. The maintenance technician was sent to an emergency room for evaluation.
